role: Independent empirical custodian; metadata only; no prediction or adjudication.

evaluation_file_choice.basis: The author-provided header designates it as the main Bell-test experiment and says one line corresponds to one trial. The text and Supplement X.A identify the final fixed nominal-angle test.
evaluation_file_choice.ordering: Use the original row order. No custodian reordering or outcome-dependent selection. The file contains no per-row timestamp.
evaluation_file_choice.other_files: fig5.txt supplies aggregate angle-scan figure data; fig2.txt supplies reconstructed/simulated density matrices. Neither supplies the designated per-trial stream. They are not optional replacements or fit inputs.
evaluation_file_choice.cutoff: Unchanged protocol rule: first accepted trials up to the protocol cap. No sample count is disclosed here.

parser_schema.validation: Every event record was checked for exactly four fields, input-bit domains and plus/minus-one output domains. No correlations or test statistics were computed.
parser_schema.packed_fpga_codes: The file is already unpacked. Supplement Table SIV separately defines FPGA codes 0=(input 0,g), 1=(input 0,e), 2=(input 1,g), 3=(input 1,e). Do not decode those packed codes a second time.

controlled_preparation.physical_qubits: Stationary superconducting transmons at nodes A and B, computational states |g>, |e>.
controlled_preparation.trigger: Deterministic preparation and complete recorded trials; no stochastic event-ready herald.
controlled_preparation.entangling_operation: Direct microwave photon exchange targets psi+ = (|ge> + |eg>)/sqrt(2).
controlled_preparation.fixed_basis_operation: Methods states that a pi/2 pulse around x at A and the corresponding phase-offset axis x+theta at B precede random basis selection; the common basis rotation is described as effectively generating phi+ = (|gg> + |ee>)/sqrt(2).
controlled_preparation.source_of_preparation: Main text Bell test; Methods Optimizing the measurement basis; Supplement IX Eq. (14). No reconstructed density matrix was used as a source input.

literal_phase_formulas.reference: Supplement IX, printed p. 16; formulas and control definitions only.
literal_phase_formulas.equation_13_location: Supplement I, printed p. 3, not Section IX. These are no-signalling definitions, not pulse-control formulas.
literal_phase_formulas.pulse_axis_definition: phi = 0 is an x-axis rotation; phi = pi/2 is a y-axis rotation.
literal_phase_formulas.preparation_sequence: pi_ge^A, (pi/2)_ef^A, f0g1^A emission, f0g1^B absorption, (pi/2)_ef^B. The first pulse phase contributes a common initial phase and is omitted in Eq. (14).
literal_phase_formulas.equation_14_kind: Prepared-state expression; the supplement does not write a complete per-setting measurement-unitary matrix here.
literal_phase_formulas.equation_15_kind: Printed theoretical expression transcribed on the parent's explicit request. No empirical S value or correlator is supplied; no additional pi/4 term has been inserted.
literal_phase_formulas.effective_phase_scope: Supplement IX combines the fixed measurement-basis rotation and optional basis-choice pulses into effective microwave phases phi_ge^A and phi_ge^B.
literal_phase_formulas.equation_16: theta = phi_ef^A + phi_ge^A - phi_f0g1^A - (phi_ef^B + phi_ge^B - phi_f0g1^B)
literal_phase_formulas.unexpanded_convention: The printed definition does not give a per-(a,b) expansion of the combined effective phi_ge values. Their relation to each literal pulse axis must be derived from the pulse sequence; matching the symbol theta alone is insufficient. No measured correlator is used to choose that relation.
literal_phase_formulas.nominal_theta_identification: Main Methods defines theta as the angle between the two measurement bases and uses it on Bob's fixed pulse; Fig. 4 uses y_theta for Bob's optional pulse. Immediately after Eq. (16), Supplement IX uses theta = theta_control + theta0 and reuses theta for the calibrated Fig. 5 phase axis. There is no separately defined theta_B and no explicit conversion between the combined Eq. (16) phase and the individual Fig. 4 pulse-axis angle. Thus the main nominal angle is not a bare uncalibrated theta_control, but equality of the total Eq. (16) phase and the individual pulse-axis angle is not established by a per-setting formula in the source.
literal_phase_formulas.transcription_check: Equations (14)-(16) checked against rendered publisher PDF and both layout/raw text extraction. The custodian did not repair notation or infer a missing phase shift.

controlled_measurement.paper_plane: The physical experiment is described in the xy plane before the fixed local basis rotations. Methods explicitly moves to the effective phi+ description; the theory role must write its fixed effect-conjugation map to the frozen real XZ family.

random_choice.0: RNG bit 0 blocks the basis-change microwave pulse.
random_choice.1: RNG bit 1 passes a pi/2_y basis-change pulse.
random_choice.reference: Supplement II, printed pp. 5-6; main Methods Random basis selection.

controlled_measurement.angle_convention: pi/2 is a Bloch-sphere rotation angle, not a state-amplitude half-angle. Microwave phase phi=0 defines x-axis rotation and phi=pi/2 defines y-axis rotation, per Supplement IX.

two_pulse_phase_scope.fixed_rotation: Methods Optimizing the measurement basis labels Alice's fixed pulse (pi/2)_x and Bob's fixed pulse (pi/2)_(x+theta).
two_pulse_phase_scope.optional_rotation: Main Fig. 4 labels Alice's optional pulse a*(pi/2)_y and Bob's optional pulse b*(pi/2)_(y_theta). These labels were checked in the rendered primary figure.
two_pulse_phase_scope.consequence: Both Bob pulse stages carry the phase-axis convention. The source does not describe theta as affecting only the fixed pre-pulse.
two_pulse_phase_scope.supplement_phrase: measurement basis rotation and basis choice pulses
two_pulse_phase_scope.reference: Main Methods; main Fig. 4; Supplement IX, printed p. 16.

readout.+1: Detected ground state |g> after the chosen rotations.
readout.-1: Detected excited state |e> after the chosen rotations.

phase_parameters.nominal_theta: -pi/4 for the designated fixed-angle experiment, as stated by the paper.
phase_parameters.theta_control: The programmed relative microwave phase is conceptually distinct from the effective nominal theta.
phase_parameters.offset_relation: Supplement IX writes theta = theta_control + theta0 and states that theta0 is an arbitrary inter-instrument phase offset requiring recalibration.
phase_parameters.fitted_offset_value: Withheld; not a permitted control-input value in this packet.
phase_parameters.independent_phase_calibration: No disjoint raw phase-calibration record or event-level provenance is supplied in the downloaded ZIP. A physical interpretation therefore requires the explicitly stated ideal nominal phase-alignment condition; this packet does not validate that condition empirically.

controlled_measurement.canonical_vector_table: Not inferred from empirical correlators. The theory role must derive the sign/orientation table from the documented pulses and chosen fixed basis convention before unsealing.

outcome_independent_admission.selection: All main-file trials; no key-only settings.
outcome_independent_admission.paper_rule: Main text includes every readout; Supplement X.A explicitly states no readout-error correction and no data post-selection.
outcome_independent_admission.readout_thresholds: Supplement VII states that integration weights and assignment thresholds are fixed before Bell test experiments.

calibration.readout_training: Supplement VII describes preparation of known g and e states for threshold/weight training prior to Bell tests.
calibration.missing_parameters: The ZIP does not supply disjoint calibration event data sufficient for independent asymmetric F0/F1 and source depolarization under the frozen calibration policy.
calibration.prohibited_substitutes: Do not use target-state tomography, fig2 density matrices, angle-scan correlators, fitted phase offsets or target event counts to supply missing calibration.

locations: Main text Bell test and Methods Optimizing the measurement basis / Random basis selection
Supplement VII: readout calibration before tests
Supplement IX: phase conventions and offset responsibility
Supplement X.A and Table SIV: raw coding and no postselection
